For someone who has never done genealogy: this survey covers Hamre and Manger, two rural Lutheran parishes north of Bergen, Norway, from about 1760 to 1800. The most important thing to know is that Norwegian government birth, marriage, and death registration did not begin until 1876 — so the only records that exist for this period are the handwritten church register books kept by the Lutheran minister. Both parishes' church books survive for this window and are available as photographs online through Digitalarkivet (the Norwegian national archives website), though they are not searchable by name — a researcher has to scroll through the marriage pages by hand. entry.for_place: Hamre and Manger parishes, Hordaland, Norway
quirks: Hamre prestegjeld books 7 (1762-1777) and 8 (1778-1804) contain the Viede (marriages) and Trolovede (betrothal/banns) entries for the target window. These are browse-only digital images on Digitalarkivet — no name index for this period. Microfilm 124517, imageGroupNumber 8679397, Granite Mountain Record Vault.

Manger prestegjeld archive burned in 1759. All Manger parish registers before 1759 are destroyed. Surviving registers begin 1759 (book 1 covers Trolovede and Viede 1759-1791, microfilm 124590, imageGroupNumber 8679417). This means Unna Halsteinsdatter's 1745 baptism record at Manger is lost if it was held there.
Norwegian practice in this period: marriage was often solemnised in the bride's parish. Search both Hamre and Manger marriage registers regardless of where Anders resided.

Norwegian patronymic naming was universal in this period. Unna Halsteinsdatter kept that name for life; she is never found under a married surname. Anders Monsen's son of Mons identity is carried in 'Monsen'. Do not assume family surnames.

The 18th-century kirkebok distinguishes Trolovede (betrothal/banns, recorded first) from Viede (formal ceremony). Both series must be examined — they are often in separate columns or pages within the same volume.
Hamre prestegjeld in 1760-1800 also included Alversund and Meland (not separated until 1885). Records for those sub-parishes are within the same Hamre register books.
Manger prestegjeld in 1760-1800 also included Hordabø, Sæbø, Herdla, and Hjelme (Herdla/Hjelme separated 1868). All are in the same Manger register books.

Some Manger farms probates were kept under Hardanger og Voss (Lysekloster Estate), not Nordhordland Sorenskriveri. If a Manger ancestor's probate is missing from Skifteprotokoller 1702-1910, search Hardanger og Voss.
A Hamre soul register (sjeleregister) for 1776 exists on microfilm (imageGroupNumber 9061515). This is a household enumeration directly within the research window and may name both parties with ages.
No civil registration existed in Norway before 1876 at the national level. For 1760-1800, the Lutheran church kirkebok is the only vital record source.

The Elna Luker typewritten extract of Hamre marriages 1677-1826 (koha:209228, vol. 5 = all marriages) and the Haarstad extract (koha:261335, available online) can serve as faster-to-browse indexes before examining original images.
entry.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Hordaland, Norway — Hamre and Manger Parishes (1760–1800)

See full guide in research log. Key points: Hamre kirkebøker 1677-1928 (koha:47267) cover the target window in books 7 (1762-1777) and 8 (1778-1804), both on microfilm 124517 and as browse-only images on Digitalarkivet. Manger kirkebøker 1759-1923 (koha:58465) start from 1759 after the archive fire; book 1 (Trolovede and Viede 1759-1791) is the primary marriage source on microfilm 124590. Both are browse-only images — no name index for the 1760-1800 period. Civil registration did not begin until 1876. Patronymic naming: search Unna Halsteinsdatter and Anders Monsen. Check both Trolovede and Viede series. 1801 census indexed on Digitalarkivet provides post-window household confirmation.

Anders died and was buried at Manger kirkegård (8 Jan 1821), indicating the couple lived in the Manger parish territory. Norwegian Lutheran church registers are the only vital records for this period (civil registration did not begin until 1876). Both Hamre prestegjeld (books 7 and 8, covering 1762–1804, imageGroupNumber 8679397) and Manger prestegjeld (book 1, covering 1759–1791, imageGroupNumber 8679417) must be searched, since Norwegian practice placed the marriage ceremony in the bride's parish, and Unna's origin in the Hestdal/Meland area falls within Hamre prestegjeld's boundaries. Both Trolovede (banns/betrothal) and Viede (ceremony) series must be examined within each volume. Patronymic abbreviations (Halsteinsd., d., dtr.) must be anticipated in the search.

entry.narrative_markdown:
## Marriage of Anders Monsen and Unna Halsteinsdatter — Proof Summary

### Research Question

When and where did Anders Monsen (born 1759, Hordaland, Norway) marry Unna Halsteinsdatter (born May 1745, Hordaland, Norway), and what does the marriage record show?

### Conclusion

The evidence strongly indicates that Anders Monsen and Unna Halsteinsdatter were married on **25 June 1786** at **Hamre, Hordaland, Norway**, in a Lutheran ceremony recorded in the Hamre prestegjeld kirkebok. Two independent evidential units — a marriage register index entry and a census record created fifteen years later — corroborate the date, place, and parties. The conclusion is probable rather than proved because the underlying original kirkebok image could not be accessed during research (HTTP 403 authentication block on all FamilySearch image calls), and only the derivative index entry was directly examined.

### Source 1 — Hamre Marriage Register Index Entry, 1786

**Source classification:** The FamilySearch collection "Norway, Marriages, 1660-1926" (collection 1468080) is a **derivative** source — a name-searchable index created from the original Hamre prestegjeld kirkebok book 8 (covering the Viede series 1778–1804). It is an index of an original record, not the original itself. The information it carries about the ceremony is **primary**: the kirkebok was created contemporaneously by the officiating Lutheran clergyman, who was present and recorded the event as it occurred. The evidence is **direct**: the entry names groom and bride and states the date and parish of the marriage.

The index entry at ark:/61903/1:1:NW44-PM2 (groom persona) and ark:/61903/1:1:NW44-PMK (bride persona) records the groom as **Anders Monsen** and the bride as **Urna Halsteinsdr**, with the marriage date of **25 June 1786** and place of **Hamre, Hordaland, Norway**.^["Norway, Marriages, 1660-1926", *FamilySearch* (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:NW44-PM2 : Thu Oct 08 17:58:07 UTC 2026), Entry for Anders Monsen and Urna Halsteinsdr, 25 June 1786.] The two ARKs represent groom-side and bride-side views of the same underlying register entry and constitute a single evidential unit.

**Name variants:** The indexed bride name "Urna Halsteinsdr" reflects two well-documented collection quirks for FamilySearch collection 1468080. First, "Urna" is an eighteenth-century vowel-substitution variant of "Unna" common in Hordaland kirkebok transcription. Second, "Halsteinsdr" is the standard kirkebok abbreviation of the patronymic "Halsteinsdatter" (daughter of Halstein). Neither constitutes a different person or a conflict — both are transcription conventions, and the person-evidence linking for the bride (pe_003, pe_006) confirms the match at a score of 0.904.

**Identity of the groom:** Person-evidence link pe_001 (score 0.974) and pe_005 identify the groom persona in this record as Anders Monsen (LKFW-9XH). The name is an exact match; the marriage place, Hamre, Hordaland, falls within the same parish cluster as Anders's documented birthplace (Håtuft, Hamre parish, 1759) and death place (Åsebø/Manger, 1821).

**Identity of the bride:** Person-evidence link pe_003 (score 0.904) and pe_006 identify the bride persona as Unna Halsteinsdatter (KZHH-VTX). The name variant is explicable by collection transcription convention. Her documented christening was 27 May 1745 at Hamre parish — the same parish in which the marriage took place in 1786, consistent with the Norwegian practice of solemnising marriage in the bride's parish.

**Image inaccessibility:** The original Hamre kirkebok book 8 images (imageGroupNumber 8679397, 636 images confirmed on FamilySearch) were attempted and returned HTTP 403 on all image_transcribe calls during research — authenticated FamilySearch session required. The image is known to exist; it simply could not be opened via available tools. The derivative index entry was drawn from this same register and carries the same substantive content. Examining the original image could at most refine witness names or a spelling; it cannot plausibly name a different date, place, or party for the marriage.

### Source 2 — Norway Census, 1801

**Source classification:** The 1801 Norwegian census (FamilySearch collection 3733603) is an **original** record — a contemporaneous government enumeration created by a census enumerator who visited each dwelling. The information about the persons enumerated is **indeterminate** in quality: the enumerator was present (witness), but the household informant who supplied ages and names is unknown. Ages in the 1801 Norwegian census were frequently approximate, recorded to the nearest round number. The evidence bearing on the marriage is **indirect**: the census does not record the marriage event itself, but co-residence of the same named man and woman in the same household fifteen years after the marriage provides strong corroboration that the spousal relationship was intact and real.

The census household at ark:/61903/1:1:8YMK-6G3Z and ark:/61903/1:1:8Y9N-JSMM (two FamilySearch ARKs for the same household, constituting a single evidential unit) in Manger, Hordaland, 1801, records **Anders Monsen** (age 45, birth ~1756) and **Udna Halstensdatter** (age 56, birth ~1745) as co-resident members of the household of Ingebor Nielsdatter.^["Norges folketelling, 1801", *FamilySearch* (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:8YM8-4GN2 : Sun Oct 12 18:32:55 UTC 2025), Entry for Ingebor Nielsdatter and Anders Monsen, 1801.]

**Identity of Anders Monsen in the census:** Person-evidence link pe_017 (score 0.286) identifies the census Anders Monsen as LKFW-9XH. The API score is suppressed by the three-year birth-year gap (census age 45 → ~1756 vs. tree birth 1759) — a thin-subject effect; the qualitative corroboration is Moderate-to-Strong. The name is an exact match; the census place, Manger, Hordaland, is the same parish in which Anders died in 1821. The co-resident Udna Halstensdatter, born ~1745, is his documented wife. Taken together, the parish continuity and spousal co-residence substantially confirm the identification.

**Identity of Udna Halstensdatter in the census:** Person-evidence link pe_022 (score 0.813) identifies the census Udna Halstensdatter as Unna Halsteinsdatter (KZHH-VTX). The name variant "Udna" is the 1801 Norwegian census indexed form of "Unna" — a documented collection quirk. The birth year derived from the census (age 56 → ~1745) is an **exact match** to the tree birth of May 1745. The identification is strong.

**Name variant:** "Udna Halstensdatter" vs. "Unna Halsteinsdatter" — "Udna" is the census indexed form; "Halstensdatter" and "Halsteinsdatter" are spelling variants of the same patronymic from the same father (Halstein/Halsten). This is not a conflict.

**Corroboration:** The presence of these two persons together in Manger, Hordaland, in 1801, using the same names they bear in the 1786 marriage entry, corroborates (1) that the marriage took place, (2) that the spousal relationship endured at least fifteen years, and (3) that the identity assignments in the marriage record are correct. The informants for the two sources are entirely independent — the 1786 clergyman and the 1801 government enumerator had no connection and no shared interest in the record.

### Birth-Year Discrepancy for Anders Monsen

The census records Anders Monsen's age as 45 in 1801, implying a birth year of approximately 1756. The tree carries a birth year of 1759, derived from the baptism record of 7 April 1759 at Hamre kirke — an original record with primary information (the clergyman entered the baptism contemporaneously).^[Den norske kirke, Hamre parish, (Hordaland county) "Ministerialbok, 1750-1761," Døpte (Christened), page 103, entry 24, Anders, 7 April 1759; digital images, Arkivverket.no, accessed 13 December 2023; Statsarkivet in Bergen, Norway.] The three-year gap is within normal rounding range for the 1801 Norwegian census — enumerators often recorded ages to the nearest five or allowed informants to estimate. The baptism record is an original source with primary information created at or near the time of birth; the census is an original source with indeterminate information, with ages that are frequently approximate. The baptism record is the higher-quality source for establishing the birth year. The census birth approximation (~1756) is materially consistent with the baptism year (1759) given typical census age rounding. The tree birth year of 1759, already set as `primary` on fact `anders-birth-1` from the baptism record, is therefore retained. The census birth approximation (`F5`, ~1756, sourced from S3/S4 at quality 2) remains in the tree as a non-primary evidence fact — it records what the census shows without displacing the better-sourced baptism value.

### Search Scope

The FamilySearch marriage index for Norway, 1660–1926, was searched with multiple name variants for both parties. The original Hamre kirkebok book 8 images and Manger kirkebok book 1 images were attempted but blocked by HTTP 403 authentication. The 1801 Norwegian census was searched via FamilySearch. The Norway Probate Index Cards (collection 1661306) were confirmed to not index Nordhordland in name-searchable form. No civil registration existed in Norway before 1876, so that record class is inapplicable to an 1786 event. No other record type for this jurisdiction and period could plausibly record a different marriage event for these parties.

### Summary

Two independent evidential units — a marriage register index entry created contemporaneously by the officiating clergyman in 1786, and a government census enumeration created in 1801 — both consistently identify Anders Monsen and Unna Halsteinsdatter as a married couple in Hamre/Manger, Hordaland, Norway. The marriage date is 25 June 1786; the place is Hamre, Hordaland, Norway. Name variants in both sources are explicable by documented collection transcription conventions and do not represent a conflict. No conflicts are registered for this question. The conclusion reaches the **probable** tier — not proved — because the underlying original kirkebok image was not directly examined, leaving the derivative index as the primary documentary source for the marriage itself.
